title: When the Parish Breaks
premise: When a drowned man washes up in Hollow Parish wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, coroner Marguerite Marchetti realizes the corpse is the 'dead' witness from a twenty-year-old case she helped bury — literally. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Marguerite must track the witness's hidden life while dodging the town elders who paid for her silence long ago. The trail leads to her own late husband's confession, revealing that her alphabetized secrets were someone else's leverage all along. In the end, Marguerite chooses justice over belonging, testifying as the statute expires and burning the parish's archive to ash.
about_author: Astrid Coldharbour spent a decade transcribing inquest records in coastal New England before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns where the dead are better documented than the living.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Marguerite performs an autopsy on a drowned stranger wearing her own missing cardigan and scarf. Her POV establishes her meticulous, guarded voice; the emotional beat is professional calm cracking into private dread when dental records match a man officially dead since 2004.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears He's Buried
chapters.summary: Marguerite quietly checks the 2004 grave — it holds the wrong skeleton. Alternating with Deputy Ilsa Voss's POV, they realize the 'witness' faked his death and someone in town knew. The beat: complicity surfacing like a body in shallow water.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Marguerite rereads her old case files and finds pages subtly altered in her own handwriting style. Flashbacks reveal how the town elders once saved her career — at a price. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing your memory was edited.

chapters.title: The Witness's Second Life
chapters.summary: Ilsa traces the victim's alias to a storage unit: photos, cash, and a list of names — including Marguerite's husband, dead five years. POV shifts to the victim via recovered cassette tapes. Beat: grief weaponized; the past was watching them all.

chapters.title: What the Elders Paid For
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Judge Aldous Renner, who admits paying for silence but denies murder — and warns her the statute expires in nine days. His POV chapter shows genuine fear of someone else pulling strings. Beat: allies and predators become indistinguishable.

chapters.title: A Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Following her own habit of knowing every grave, Marguerite finds a fresh unmarked plot behind the chapel matching the witness's mother. Exhumation reveals evidence the witness hid there himself. Beat: the dead leading the living; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: The final cassette is her husband's voice confessing he falsified the autopsy that declared the witness dead. Marguerite listens alone through the night. Beat: betrayal and terrible tenderness — he protected her, and damned her.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Then None
chapters.summary: With three days left, the true killer — town clerk Doris Halloway, whose family the original crime destroyed — tries to burn the archive with Marguerite inside. Ilsa's POV rescue sequence. Beat: survival at last costing something real.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax: Marguerite takes the stand as the statute expires at midnight, reading her husband's confession aloud while Doris is arrested for two murders twenty years apart. Beat: justice outside the law finally entering it; belonging forfeited.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ashes
chapters.summary: Resolution: Marguerite burns the sealed archive herself, resigns, and plants a marker for the witness under his real name. Final image: a town that no longer knows her, and a woman who finally knows herself. Beat: costly peace.
